title: Platform engineering team wiki & playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page is the canonical team wiki and operational playbook for Redwood Inference's Platform Engineering team. It centralizes systems & services descriptions, how-tos, dashboards and alerting guidance, runbooks, retrospective notes, and our short-term roadmap. The intent is a single, searchable reference that oncall engineers, new hires, and partner teams can rely on during routine operations and incidents.

Scope
- Systems & services: SLO owners and high level architecture for core platform services (service catalog, deployment control plane, metrics pipeline, auth/proxy, CI/CD).
- How-tos: common operational tasks, onboarding scripts, and deployment recipes.
- Dashboards & alerts: recommended dashboards, alert thresholds, and escalation paths.
- Runbooks: step-by-step procedures for common incidents and maintenance.
- Retrospectives: links and short summaries for recent postmortems and operational improvements.
- Roadmap: prioritized initiatives for the next two quarters that directly impact run reliability and developer productivity.

Ownership & RACI
- Platform Systems (service catalog, control plane): Owner — Platform Core (team lead: Marcus Chen). R: Platform Core, A: Head of Eng Platform, C: Eng SRE, I: Product.
- Observability (metrics, logging, tracing): Owner — Observability Squad (lead: Sofia Nguyen). R: Observability, A: Platform Lead, C: Eng SRE, I: All teams.
- Runbooks & Alerts: Owner — Oncall & Runbooks subteam. R: Oncall team, A: Platform Lead, C: Incident Response, I: Product/Support.

How-tos (common tasks)
1) Deploy a service to the platform
- Preflight: run `platformctl lint` and verify CI green.
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic for 30 minutes, check latency P95 and error rate.
- Promote: bump traffic 25% every 15m if metrics stable.
- Rollback: `platformctl rollback --to <previous-tag>` and open a rollback ticket.

2) Add a dashboard panel
- Location: Grafana dashboard folder `redwood/platform/` — create a new folder if necessary.
- Panel template: use the standard card with metric name, unit, short description, and link to runbook.
- Review: add Observability reviewer tag and request review via Slack channel #observability-reviews.

3) Create or tune an alert
- Use alert frequency and noise minimization checklist: ensure the signal ties to user impact, add a 5m aggregator where appropriate, include suppression during deploy windows.
- Required fields in alert definition: alert name, description (user impact), owner (team/contact), runbook link, severity (sev1/sev2/sev3).

Dashboards & Alerts (standards)
- Dashboards: each service must have a minimum dashboard covering: request rate (RPS), p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx split), CPU/GPU utilization, queue/backlog size, and key business metrics mapped to segments (customer, region).
- Naming convention: `svc.<service_name>.<env>.<dashboard>`. Example: `svc.control-plane.prod.overview`.
- SLOs: Services should declare a service level objective documented in the metadata header of the dashboard. Example: availability SLO 99.9% monthly, latency p95 < 150ms for short requests.
- Alerting thresholds (recommended):
  - Availability: trigger when rolling 5m availability < 99.5% AND incident duration > 5m.
  - Error rate: trigger when 5m error rate > 0.5% AND increase is >2x baseline.
  - Latency: trigger when p95 latency > 2x expected SLO for 5m.
  - Resource saturation: node GPU/CPU > 85% sustained for 10m.

Alert routing & escalation
- Sev1 (platform-wide outage): page platform-oncall + oncall escalation to SRE lead. Follow sev1 runbook (link below).
- Sev2 (service impacting subset of customers): page service owner + platform-oncall; if unresolved for 30m escalate to Platform Tech Lead.
- Sev3 (degraded performance): notify service owner via Slack thread and create ticket.
- Pager duties: primary oncall owns first 30m actionables; handover to secondary after 45m if unresolved.

Runbooks (templates & examples)
- Template fields: symptom, impact assessment, quick mitigations, detailed diagnosis steps, mitigation code snippets, verification, post-incident tasks.

Example: Sev1 control-plane outage (abridged)
- Symptom: control-plane API returns 503 for >30% of requests for 5m.
- Quick mitigations:
  1. Confirm alert and check Grafana: control-plane.prod.overview.
  2. Check leader election and primary replicas: `kubectl get pods -n control-plane`.
  3. If pods restarting, collect logs `kubectl logs --since=10m` and tag incident.
  4. Scale replicas: `kubectl scale deploy/control-plane --replicas=3` (temporary).
- Diagnosis steps: check recent deploys, config changes, upstream dependency health (datastore, auth service).
- Rollback criteria: if error rate or latency worsens following a deploy and no external dependency issue, rollback to previous image.
- Verification: confirm p95 latency and availability return within SLOs for 10m.
- Post-incident: file postmortem within 72 hours and attach runbook updates.

Retrospectives & continuous improvement
- Every operational incident that meets the postmortem threshold (any sev1 or repeated sev2s) gets a documented retrospective with: timeline, contributing factors, mitigations, owner for each action item, and target completion date.
- Runbook reviews: runbooks are reviewed quarterly by the Oncall & Runbooks subteam. Changes must include a short rationale and reviewer signoff.
- Reliability initiatives: we prioritize work that reduces toil (automation), reduces blast radius (isolation), or improves observability. Each initiative has a success metric attached (eg. alert noise reduction by 40% over 90 days).

Roadmap (next two quarters)
- Q3 2026 priorities:
  1. Observability rewrite: migrate metrics pipeline to Prometheus Remote Write in a multi-tenant, cost-optimized cluster. Owner: Observability.
  2. Canary automation: ship `platformctl canary` to automate staged rollouts with automated metric checks. Owner: Platform Core.
  3. Runbook library audit: complete audit and retire/refresh stale runbooks (target: 100% reviewed). Owner: Oncall Subteam.
- Q4 2026 priorities:
  1. Alert rationalization: reduce noisy alerts by 50% via tuning and smart deduplication.
  2. Self-serve dashboards: templates and onboarding flow for product teams to create dashboards with required minimums.

Onboarding checklist for new platform engineers
- Read the platform architecture overview (link in related pages).
- Complete sandbox deployment lab and deploy test service.
- Pair on first oncall rotation with senior buddy.
- Review top 10 runbooks and edit one to fix a documentation gap.

Operational hygiene (must do items)
- Keep runbooks in sync: update runbook metadata with owner and last reviewed date after any change.
- Tag dashboards with an SLO and runbook link.
- Add post-deploy suppression windows for major launches.
- Triaging SLA: support tickets labeled `platform-impact` must be acknowledged within 2 business hours.

References & related pages
- Platform systems & services playbook (see related pages).
- Observability standards and SLO library.
- Incident response and escalation playbook.

Appendix: example alert JSON (policy snippet)
```json
{
  "alert": "control_plane_high_error_rate",
  "description": "5m error rate > 0.5% and >2x baseline",
  "owner": "team:platform-core",
  "severity": "sev2",
  "runbook": "confluence/eng-platform/control-plane-runbook-2025"
}
```

Contact points
- Platform Slack channels: #platform-oncall, #platform-ops, #observability-reviews.
- Pager duty: platform-oncall schedule (see internal roster).

If you notice outdated content or missing runbooks, please file a doc request in #platform-docs or open a PR against the team wiki.
